memory_update.text: MP is the reference leader for U.S.-listed mine-to-magnet exposure, but should be used as benchmark rather than the main underfollowed discovery candidate.
USAR is a direct public magnet-manufacturing challenger to verify through Stillwater output, customer qualification, and non-Chinese feedstock chain evidence.
UUUU is a second-order but high-relevance feedstock/oxide candidate because its NdPr and dysprosium oxide qualification for magnet use links White Mesa to the compliant magnet bottleneck.

UURAF belongs in a speculative shadow lane: strong thematic fit as a DoD-funded heavy rare-earth separation processor, but survival to later layers requires proof of commercial scale and magnet-maker qualification.

For this node, later-layer diligence should prioritize qualification evidence over nominal capacity: feedstock origin, separated oxide purity, metal/alloy conversion, magnet-line validation, defense/customer approval, and binding offtake.

Need a separate pass for private but strategically important magnet makers and customers such as Vulcan Elements, eVAC Magnetics, ReElement, GM, defense primes and drone/actuator suppliers; they may determine which public upstream suppliers actually get qualified.
MP should be retained as the reference anchor for U.S. mine-to-magnet integration, but it is not the primary underfollowed discovery target.
USAR is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the rare-earth magnet qualification node because it reports Stillwater magnet commissioning plus metal/alloy/feedstock capabilities.
UUUU should be tracked as a magnet-grade rare-earth oxide supplier rather than only as a uranium name; qualification of NdPr and Dy oxides is the key signal.
AREC/ReElement is a below-300m speculative exception; do not promote beyond Layer 1 unless SEC filings and customer/offtake evidence confirm scale, ownership economics, and qualification.

For this node, prioritize proof of compliant feedstock origin, heavy rare-earth availability, metal/alloy conversion, sintered NdFeB production, and customer qualification over generic rare-earth resource size.

Need a follow-up pass on non-US-listed but relevant comparables such as Neo Performance Materials, Lynas, private Vulcan Elements, Arnold Magnetic Technologies, and HyProMag to benchmark U.S.-listed candidates.
MP is the reference anchor for U.S. integrated rare-earth magnet capacity; do not let it crowd out smaller qualification/feedstock candidates in later layers.
USAR is a priority underfollowed candidate for Layer 2 because federal support and planned NdFeB/metals capacity map directly to the non-Chinese-feedstock magnet qualification node.
UUUU should be tracked as an oxide/feedstock qualification gate rather than a magnet manufacturer; key survival test is magnet-maker/OEM validation of NdPr and heavy REE oxides at scale.

NB is a speculative shadow candidate: domestic magnetic rare-earth oxide optionality exists, but it should not survive later layers without financing, feasibility, offtake, and downstream qualification evidence.

Need a later pass on private or non-U.S.-listed magnet makers such as Vulcan Elements, Noveon, e-VAC/Vacuumschmelze, Ucore, Neo Performance, and Lynas as customer/supplier anchors even if they are not U.S.-listed common-stock candidates.
Add MP as reference anchor for U.S. integrated rare-earth mine-to-magnet capacity, but do not let it crowd out underfollowed magnet-channel and oxide-feedstock candidates.
Add USAR as underfollowed direct magnet qualification candidate; monitor Stillwater Phase 1a customer orders, feedstock provenance, Arnold distribution partnership, and execution/IP risk.

Add CODI as hidden-asset exposure through Arnold Magnetic Technologies; the relevant diligence is Arnold revenue, defense qualification, SmCo/NdFeB capability, and whether Arnold is material to consolidated CODI.
Add UUUU as upstream oxide/feedstock chokepoint candidate; evidence must verify whether Energy Fuels material is qualified into magnet metal/alloy/magnet supply chains.
For this node, customer qualification and compliant provenance are higher-signal than headline mine capacity or nominal magnet tonnage.

Need a later Layer 2 pass on private or foreign-listed magnet makers and processors such as Neo Performance Materials, Vulcan Elements, Niron Magnetics, REalloys, Arnold standalone operations, and Less Common Metals because US-listed coverage may miss key qualification bottlenecks.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expanded the direct public-company universe around compliant rare-earth magnet qualification. The strongest direct exposures are U.S. mine-to-magnet or oxide-to-magnet chains where the evidence includes actual NdFeB magnet production, government funding, customer qualification, or non-Chinese feedstock validation. The list intentionally separates reference leaders from underfollowed or speculative small/mid-cap exposure. No trading recommendation is implied. Layer 1B expands the universe around a policy-driven rare-earth magnet qualification chokepoint. The scarce layer appears to be qualified oxide-to-metal-to-alloy-to-NdFeB magnet capacity that can document non-Chinese feedstock for defense and dual-use customers, not merely rare-earth mining tonnage. The two-lane list keeps MP Materials as the obvious reference anchor, then prioritizes USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels, and American Resources/ReElement as underfollowed or speculative public-market ways to track compliant feedstock, separation, magnet-grade oxides, recycling, and domestic magnet-chain qualification. Expanded the universe around the chokepoint that defense-relevant rare-earth magnet capacity may be constrained less by nominal ex-China magnet tonnage and more by qualified oxide-to-metal-to-alloy-to-NdFeB magnet chains using compliant non-Chinese feedstock. The reference lane is MP Materials because it is the clearest U.S. integrated mine-to-magnet anchor with DoD support.
